title: Boundary principal divisors are unchanged by algebraically closed base change
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension]. Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], and choose a smooth proper connected compactification $j:C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ with finite boundary $S=\overline C\setminus C$ [lem-sc-compactification]. Put $\overline C'=\overline C\times_k k'$, $C'=C\times_k k'$, and $S'=\overline C'\setminus C'$. Using divisors as in [def-sc-divisor], each point of $S$ is $k$-rational and its base change is a single point of $S'$, which gives a canonical identification $\iota:\bigoplus_{P\in S}\mathbf Z[P]\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{P'\in S'}\mathbf Z[P']$. For every $u\in\mathcal O_C(C)^\times$, with pullback $u'\in\mathcal O_{C'}(C')^\times$ along $C'\to C$, the boundary part of $\operatorname{div}(u')$ on $\overline C'$ is $\iota$ of the boundary part of $\operatorname{div}(u)$ on $\overline C$; and $\iota$ maps the subgroup of boundary divisors of units on $C$ onto the subgroup of boundary divisors of units on $C'$.

proof.text: Write $X=\overline C$ and $X'=\overline C'$. By [lem-sc-pic-affine-base-change-compatibility] (1), $X'$ is a smooth proper connected compactification of $C'$ whose boundary is $S'=\{P':P\in S\}$, where each $P\in S$ (a $k$-rational closed point, $k$ being algebraically closed) pulls back to a single $k'$-point $P'$. Hence $P\mapsto P'$ is a bijection $S\to S'$, and it induces the canonical identification $\iota:\bigoplus_{P\in S}\mathbf Z[P]\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{P'\in S'}\mathbf Z[P']$.

source.place: Affine-case proof, compactification and boundary setup

proof.text: Let $u\in\mathcal O_C(C)^\times$ and view $u$ as a nonzero rational function on the proper curve $X$. At each $P\in S$ the coefficient of $[P]$ in $\operatorname{div}(u)$ is the normalized order $v_P(u)$ [def-sc-divisor]. By [lem-sc-local-dvr-base-change] the pullback $u'$ has $v_{P'}(u')=v_P(u)$. Hence the boundary part of $\operatorname{div}(u')$ is $\iota$ of the boundary part of $\operatorname{div}(u)$.

Let $L$ and $L'$ be the subgroups of boundary divisors of units on $C$ and on $C'$. Step 2 gives $\iota(L)\subseteq L'$. Conversely let $D'=\sum_{P\in S}n_P[P']\in L'$ and $D=\sum_{P\in S}n_P[P]$ on $X$. Since $D'$ is the divisor of a unit on $C'$, it is principal on $X'$, so $\mathcal O_{X'}(D')$ is trivial [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve], and $\deg D=\deg D'=0$ [lem-sc-deg-principal-zero]. Since $\mathcal O_X(P)$ pulls back to $\mathcal O_{X'}(P')$ for each $P\in S$ [lem-sc-pic-affine-base-change-compatibility] (1), $\mathcal O_X(D)$ pulls back to $\mathcal O_{X'}(D')$, so the class of $\mathcal O_X(D)$ in $\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)$ maps to $0$ in $\operatorname{Pic}^0(X')$. By [lem-sc-pic-affine-base-change-compatibility] (3) this pullback is the Jacobian base-change map $J_X(k)\to J_{X'}(k')=J_X(k')$ [lem-sc-genus-invariant], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability], which is injective because $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an epimorphism (so $Y(k)\to Y(k')$ is injective for every $k$-scheme $Y$). Hence $\mathcal O_X(D)$ is trivial, and $D=\operatorname{div}(f)$ for some $f\in k(X)^*$ [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve]. Then $v_Q(f)=0$ at every closed point $Q\in C$, so $f\in\mathcal O_C(C)^\times$ by exactness of $0\to\mathbf G_m\to j_*\mathbf G_{m,\eta}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}}\bigoplus_x i_{x*}\mathbf Z$ on sections over $C$ [lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general], and $D\in L$. Thus $L'=\iota(L)$.
